surprise_packets.expected_outcome: When Kevin's resolved escalation text clearly says the work is complete, working as needed, deferred for later human/manual timing, or only needs follow-up if a real issue remains, Ralph should recommend closure or review parking rather than relaunching another worker loop.
surprise_packets.actual_outcome: When a worker escalates because it is blocked or unsure whether to close, require a short concrete request that states the decision Kevin can answer, the recommended end goal, and the minimum unblock condition.

likely_causal_hypotheses.formalization_hint: Closeout evaluator can treat resolved human terminal/defer signals as evidence for closure or parking, not automatic relaunch.
Planner/reviewer can require concrete_request, recommended_end_goal, and minimum_unblock_condition fields before treating an escalation as ready for human review.

surprise_packets.expected_outcome: The running system may execute from a dirty or shared checkout (many modified/untracked files), so "the code is merged" does not imply "the running system runs it." Verify the running sink's exact source revision/state before trusting that landed changes are live.
surprise_packets.actual_outcome: A recovery mechanism only improves reliability when it can verify that recovery actually occurred.

likely_causal_hypotheses.formalization_hint: ASP/PDDL: require verified_running_source(Sink) before concluding landed_code_is_live(Sink); a dirty_checkout(Sink) fact blocks deploy_trust until re-verification.
ASP integrity constraint can reject recovery actions without a postcondition health proof.
